correctness.rationale: For finite interval orders (2+2-free strict posets), strict successor sets are nested; ordering elements by decreasing successor counts u makes the predecessor set of any vertex y exactly the first d(y) elements, and a tie in u cannot split the initial segment. Thus the (d,u) multiset reconstructs the relation up to isomorphism; additionally nested predecessor sets imply equal (d,u) precisely identical strict neighborhoods and automorphism orbits. A C² counting sentence ∃^{=m}x[(∃^{=a}y y<x)∧(∃^{=b}y x<y)] of quantifier rank 2 detects each pair multiplicity; a rank-one sentence cannot compare distinct elements, as witnessed by the two-vertex chain vs antichain. Allowed outgoing-degree vectors are staircase partitions a_i≤n−i (Catalan), realized by terminal-suffix strict successor sets; transitivity holds. Fishburn upper-triangular nonnegative matrices with all positive row/column sums encode interval orders and each degree profile fixes both margins, giving the displayed coefficient of ∏_{i≤j}(1−x_i y_j)^{-1}. Independently computed the two 4-element Fishburn matrices with identical outgoing degree multiset [2,1,0,0] but distinct paired-degree profiles; minimality through n≤3 follows the small-staircase margin cases.
